key_insight: Adjusting ultrasound intensity enables remote, noncontact switching between suppressing natural convection for heat retention and inducing forced convection for cooling.
engineering_relevance: Target-selective acoustic airflow could provide virtual insulation or cooling for food, beverages, manufacturing processes, and laboratory systems.
method: Direct an ultrasonic beam at a heat-source surface to generate acoustic streaming.
Adjust ultrasonic output intensity to accelerate or decelerate surface airflow.
Control convective heat escape without contacting the object.
evidence_signal: Experiments demonstrated switching between heat retention and cooling by changing ultrasonic output intensity, although the abstract reports no quantitative performance metrics.
watch_item: Practical deployment requires validation of operating range, energy efficiency, and ultrasound exposure limits in room environments.
paper_title: Remote and Noncontact Acceleration and Suppression of Heat Convection on Object Surfaces using Intensity-Adjusted Acoustic Streaming
